selected_subject.anchorage_tie: STAK Energy is headquartered in Anchorage, Alaska (stak.energy states 'Based in Anchorage and built with American grit at its core'). Mahoney is Anchorage-bowl-based as founder and CEO of the Anchorage-domiciled corporate entity, even though the project site is on the North Slope.

selected_decision.what_happened: The Alaska Department of Natural Resources on May 12, 2026 issued a preliminary decision to lease 715.4 acres of North Slope land to STAK Energy, issuing a preliminary, formal determination that the project is in the state's 'best interest.' STAK Energy has proposed a $500 million AI and cloud computing data center campus on Alaska's Arctic North Slope. The project could ultimately produce up to three gigawatts of power for its own use, generated by an on-site natural gas power plant. STAK filed the lease application with DNR in November 2025; DNR solicited competing bids and received none. The public comment period runs through June 15, 2026.
selected_decision.binary_owned: Mahoney, as Founder and CEO, filed the North Slope land lease application with DNR in November 2025 and drove the company to a preliminary 'best interest' determination on May 12, 2026, committing STAK Energy to a 50-year state lease track and a $500M off-grid natural-gas-powered AI data center development path, choosing that model over grid-tied or alternative-site approaches.
selected_decision.ak_consequence: Energy and data infrastructure sector; $500M capital commitment; up to 3 GW of off-grid power capacity; 50-year land lease on Alaska state North Slope acreage; peak construction workforce of approximately 1,500 jobs and roughly 60 permanent positions; public comment period open through June 15, 2026 with final DNR lease decision pending. Sets the precedent for whether Alaska becomes a large-scale AI compute host state using stranded North Slope natural gas.

corroborating_sources.verification_note: Returned HTTP 403 on revalidation; treat as surfaced-but-unverified for this cycle

structural_read: MEDIOCRE-TO-SPECULATIVE. The DNR preliminary best-interest determination is a real milestone, but the underlying project has structural gaps that make the 'historic moment for Alaska AI' framing premature. STAK has no disclosed outside equity financing, no named anchor tenant or offtake agreement, and no interconnection agreement with any grid operator because it proposes to be entirely off-grid, which is itself an unproven model at gigawatt scale. The natural gas supply case (stranded North Slope gas plus Arctic free cooling) is the genuine strategic logic, but Cook Inlet gas decline is the wrong analogy here. North Slope gas is abundant but pipelines to move it are absent, meaning the project's power supply depends on Mahoney building or contracting a gas gathering and processing infrastructure that has not been announced. Most consequentially, this is the same site Mahoney previously pitched for crypto mining, and STAK officials declined to answer specific questions from multiple reporters. DNR's preliminary determination is a procedural step that any unopposed application can achieve; the hard test is whether STAK closes project financing before the public comment period ends and a final lease is executed. The desk reads this as a credible strategic bet on a real Alaska comparative advantage (stranded gas plus cold climate) executed with a notable lack of transparency about who is actually funding it.
forward_implication: The DNR public comment period closes June 15, 2026. The next binary Mahoney owns is whether STAK can respond to comments substantively and move DNR toward a final lease award, and separately, whether the company discloses a lead equity investor or anchor tenant before the final lease is signed. Watch for any project financing announcement, an interconnect or gas supply agreement filing, or a competing lease challenge during the comment period. If no financing is disclosed by the time the comment period closes, the project's credibility deteriorates sharply.
